headline: Federal agencies flagged a fourth exploited SharePoint flaw for urgent patching as attackers turned trusted AI tools and a 314-million-install browser extension into fresh paths into corporate networks.

emerging_trends.text: Malware such as Sandworm_Mode and a prompt-injection flaw in Microsoft's Azure DevOps MCP server show attackers folding trusted AI coding tools into their operations, where malicious steps look identical to a developer's normal work.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Attackers Live Off the AI Toolchain

emerging_trends.text: A vulnerability in the Adobe Acrobat browser extension carried by 314 million installs let any website siphon WhatsApp Web chats, underscoring how everyday browser plug-ins have become a soft path to a victim's private messages.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Adobe Acrobat Extension Flaw Exposed WhatsApp Web Data

emerging_trends.text: Attackers exploiting the fourth SharePoint flaw of the month steal IIS machine keys to survive patching, a persistence trick that pushed CISA to add CVE-2026-50522 to its must-fix catalog.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Fourth SharePoint Flaw CVE-2026-50522 Hits CISA's Exploited List

topics.title: Fourth SharePoint Flaw CVE-2026-50522 Hits CISA's Exploited List
topics.latest_developments: CISA added CVE-2026-50522 and Check Point SmartConsole flaw CVE-2026-16232 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on July 22, 2026, after watchTowr's honeypots caught attackers stealing IIS machine keys through the SharePoint bug once public exploit code appeared.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-50522 marks the fourth Microsoft SharePoint deserialization flaw attackers have exploited in a month. They run code on on-premises servers and lift the IIS machine keys that preserve access after a patch, so administrators must patch and rotate those keys.

sources.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
Another SharePoint RCE exploited: Patch, then rotate your machine keys (CVE-2026-50522)
Fourth SharePoint Vulnerability Exploited in Past Month's Wave of Attacks

topics.title: Adobe Acrobat Extension Flaw Exposed WhatsApp Web Data
topics.latest_developments: Guardio Labs disclosed HermeticReader, tracked as CVE-2026-48294, a now-patched flaw chain in the Adobe Acrobat Chrome extension and its 314 million installs that let any malicious website silently read a victim's WhatsApp Web messages and contacts.
topics.summary: A user only had to visit a booby-trapped page for an attacker to exfiltrate WhatsApp Web chats and contacts through the Adobe extension. Adobe has patched the flaw, and users should update the extension.

sources.title: Adobe Acrobat Extension Flaw Let Malicious Sites Read WhatsApp Web Data
Flaw in Adobe Extension With 300M Installs Enabled WhatsApp Data Theft
Adobe Chrome extension flaw let sites access private WhatsApp chats

topics.title: Attackers Live Off the AI Toolchain
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading detailed Sandworm_Mode, malware that hides inside trusted AI tools and workflows so its actions resemble ordinary developer activity, as researchers disclosed a flaw in Microsoft's official Azure DevOps MCP server that lets one invisible pull-request comment hijack a reviewer's AI coding agent.
topics.summary: Attackers increasingly abuse the AI development toolchain itself—coding agents, MCP servers, and generated code. Analysis of vibe-coded applications turned up 434 exploitable flaws, and the trend erases the line between malicious steps and normal automation, so teams need least-privilege controls on every agent.

sources.title: Attackers Are Learning to Live Off the AI Toolchain
Microsoft Azure DevOps MCP Flaw Lets Hidden PR Comments Hijack AI Review Agents
Vibe-Coded Apps Riddled With Exploitable Security Flaws

topics.title: Suno, Chick-fil-A, and Upbound Breaches Surface
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported hackers leaked names, emails, phone numbers, passwords, and financial data pulled from AI music generator Suno and rewards platform Paidwork, hitting tens of millions of accounts, while Chick-fil-A began notifying customers whose accounts fell to credential-stuffing and Upbound Group said thieves turned stolen data into $13 million in fraudulent Acima leases.
topics.summary: Four consumer and fintech brands disclosed intrusions the same day. Affected users should reset reused passwords, watch for fraud, and turn on multi-factor authentication.

sources.title: Suno, Paidwork Data Breaches Affect Tens of Millions of Accounts
Chick-fil-A discloses data breach after credential stuffing attacks
Upbound says hack caused $13 million in fraudulent Acima leases

topics.title: CISA 2015 Renewal and France's Under-15 Social Media Ban
topics.latest_developments: The US House folded a 10-year renewal of the CISA 2015 cyber information-sharing law into its fiscal 2027 defense authorization bill, France's Parliament voted to bar children under 15 from social media, and the Justice Department's Operation Offsides seized more than 1,000 domains that streamed FIFA World Cup 2026 matches without a license.
topics.summary: Lawmakers and prosecutors moved on three fronts—liability protections for sharing threat data, youth online safety, and piracy enforcement. The CISA 2015 renewal restores the legal cover companies rely on to exchange threat indicators with the government.

sources.title: Extension of CISA 2015 info-sharing protections passes as part of House's defense bill
French Parliament greenlights social media ban for under-15s
US seizes over 1,000 domains used for illegal World Cup 2026 streams

topics.title: South Korea Diplomatic Academy Breach Exposes Diplomats
topics.latest_developments: South Korea disclosed that intruders spent ten months inside the National Diplomatic Academy's online education system and stole personal data on current and former Ministry of Foreign Affairs staff, including diplomats posted overseas.
topics.summary: The breach exposed a sensitive roster of South Korean foreign-service personnel worldwide, a prime target for espionage. Affected diplomats face heightened phishing and impersonation risk.

sources.title: South Korea discloses data breach impacting diplomats worldwide

business_politics.title: Trump Threatens to Bomb Iran's Bridges and Power Plants
business_politics.latest_developments: Trump announced July 22 that the United States will strike Iranian bridges and power plants for every Iranian attack on a ship, surged troops, medics, and weaponry toward the Middle East, and paid respects at Dover to four service members killed in recent attacks.
business_politics.summary: The war between the United States and Iran centers on control of the Strait of Hormuz; Trump's retaliatory policy and force buildup signal a planned escalation, and the House passed a Republican-only $95 billion package to fund the fight.

sources.title: U.S. Surges Forces Toward Middle East, Giving Trump Options to Expand Iran War
Trump Says U.S. Will Bomb Iran's Power Plants, Bridges if Tehran Strikes Ships
Trump threatens to destroy Iranian bridges and power plants

business_politics.title: U.S. and Saudi Arabia Seal Nuclear Pact That Could Allow Enrichment
business_politics.latest_developments: Trump approved a landmark civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia on July 22, terms that could hand the kingdom uranium-enrichment capability and drew warnings the deal lacks proliferation safeguards.
business_politics.summary: The agreement promises large profits for American nuclear firms, and critics—including a Wall Street Journal editorial—warn its missing enrichment and reprocessing controls risk spreading nuclear weapons capability across the Middle East.

sources.title: Trump Approves Landmark Nuclear Deal With Saudi Arabia in Big Win for Kingdom
US and Saudi Arabia agree landmark nuclear energy pact

business_politics.title: Treasury Selloff Drives Yields Toward 2026 Highs
business_politics.latest_developments: A government-bond selloff pushed the 2-year Treasury yield to its highest level in more than a year on July 22 and lifted the 10-year yield close to its 2026 high, tightening financial conditions as oil climbs.
business_politics.summary: Rising yields raise borrowing costs for consumers and companies and pressure equities; the move comes as elevated bond yields across major economies and Middle East supply fears reshape the rate outlook.

sources.title: 2-Year Treasury Yield Highest In Over a Year
What Surging Bond Yields Mean for Consumers and Markets

business.title: WVU Medicine Settles DEA Narcotics Case for $4.17 Million
business.latest_developments: West Virginia University Health System agreed to pay $4.17 million to settle a U.S. Department of Justice civil case over controlled-substance oversight failures at several registered facilities, TribLive reported July 22.
business.summary: The system, which recently struck a deal to acquire the five-hospital Independence Health System serving Westmoreland and Butler counties, resolved allegations of lax narcotics recordkeeping across multiple sites.

sources.title: WVU Medicine to pay $4.17M in DEA settlement over narcotics oversight

business.title: State Grant to Restore Etna's Union Hotel
business.latest_developments: A $500,000 state grant will help upgrade the historic Union Hotel in the heart of Etna, TribLive reported July 22.
business.summary: The community redevelopment award funds restoration of the long-standing Union Hotel building in Etna, the borough along Pine Creek just north of Pittsburgh.

sources.title: Community redevelopment grant to aid in restoration of Etna's historic Union Hotel

around_town.title: Parkway East to Reopen by Mid-Next Week
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT now expects to reopen the Parkway East by the middle of next week after crews slid the new Commercial Street Bridge into place ahead of schedule, and Transportation Secretary Mike Carroll called the swap a "stunning achievement" on July 22.
around_town.summary: The Commercial Street Bridge replacement outside the Squirrel Hill Tunnel closed the Parkway East for a project first set to run 25 days with an August 3 reopening; the accelerated pace moves that up.

sources.title: Parkway East expected to reopen by the middle of next week with replacement of Commercial Street Bridge
Parkway East expected to reopen next week, PennDOT says

around_town.title: Downtown Tax-Diversion Plan Splits City Council
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Council split sharply July 22 over a proposal to divert future tax revenue to Downtown redevelopment and transit projects, advancing the multimillion-dollar plan even as resident backlash and opposition persist.
around_town.summary: The tax-increment plan, a TRID, would channel future revenue into Downtown Pittsburgh revitalization and transit work; council members remain divided as residents object to the diversion.

sources.title: Deep fissures split Pittsburgh officials over proposed Downtown tax diversion
Multimillion-dollar Downtown Pittsburgh revitalization plan advances, but opposition remains

around_town.title: New Brentwood Elementary Opening Delayed
around_town.latest_developments: The new Brentwood Elementary School will not be ready for the coming school year, delayed by weather and a labor shortage, WPXI reported July 22.
around_town.summary: Brentwood Borough, south of Pittsburgh, built the new elementary building expecting to open it for 2026-27, but construction setbacks pushed the timeline back.

sources.title: New Brentwood Elementary School's opening delayed

events.title: Sharif Bey 'Homecoming' at the Andy Warhol Museum
events.latest_developments: The Andy Warhol Museum is showing "Homecoming," an exhibition bringing celebrated ceramic sculptor Sharif Bey back to Pittsburgh, where his career began, the Post-Gazette reported July 22.
events.summary: "Homecoming" gathers work by Sharif Bey, a sculptor who came up in Pittsburgh, at the Andy Warhol Museum on the North Shore.

sources.title: 'Homecoming' exhibition brings a celebrated Pittsburgh sculptor back to where it all began

events.title: Trundle Manor Shows Its Oddities in Swissvale
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's off-the-beaten-path feature July 20 spotlighted Trundle Manor, a macabre house of curiosities in Swissvale.
events.summary: Trundle Manor, a private museum in Swissvale run by its collectors, displays a weird, quirky trove of oddities open to visitors.

sources.title: Off the beaten path: Macabre Trundle Manor in Swissvale explores the weird, quirky

around_teams.title: Debating T.J. Watt's Trade Value
around_teams.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette video segment July 22 asked whether Steelers edge rusher T.J. Watt would still command a first-round pick in a trade, weighing the rumors swirling around the star pass rusher.
around_teams.summary: The discussion turns on Watt, the Steelers' All-Pro outside linebacker, and whether his age or contract have cooled the market for him as offseason speculation continues.

sources.title: WATCH: Is the Steelers' T.J. Watt not worth a first-round pick in a trade anymore?

around_teams.title: Hiles Urges Pirates to Buy at the Deadline
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles argued July 22 that the Pirates should keep their promises and "push chips in" at the trade deadline, pressing general manager Ben Cherington and owner Bob Nutting to add talent now.
around_teams.summary: With the Pirates clinging to wild-card hopes, Hiles called for win-now moves, a shift from his earlier stance that the club hold onto Oneil Cruz.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: It's time for the Pirates to keep their promises and push chips in at the trade deadline

around_teams.title: Rookies Keep the Pirates' Playoff Hopes Alive
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette detailed July 22 how rookies, including outfielder Esmerlyn Valdez and Billy Cook, have propped up a Pirates lineup gutted by injuries and kept the postseason push going.
around_teams.summary: Injuries thinned the Pirates roster; young players stepping into everyday roles have sustained the club's wild-card chase through the summer.
